stem.text: The temperature of a cup of coffee is modeled by the differentiable function \( H \), where \( H(t) \) is measured in degrees Celsius and \( t \) is measured in minutes. Selected values of \( H(t) \) are given in the table. \( \begin{array}{c|cccc} t \text{ (minutes)} & 0 & 3 & 7 & 12 \\ \hline H(t) \text{ (degrees Celsius)} & 90 & 78 & 66 & 57 \end{array} \)

parts.prompt: Use the data in the table to approximate \( H'(5) \). Show the computations that lead to your answer, and indicate units of measure.

worked_solution.text: Use the two table values that bracket t = 5.
Units are the output units per input unit.

points.criterion: Gives -3 supported by a difference quotient over the interval from t = 3 to t = 7.
Gives the units degrees Celsius per minute.

parts.prompt: Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( H'(5) \) in the context of the problem, using your answer to part (a).
parts.answer_latex: \text{at } t = 5 \text{ the temperature is decreasing at about 3 degrees Celsius per minute}

worked_solution.text: A negative rate means the temperature is falling at that instant.
worked_solution.latex: \text{At } t = 5 \text{ minutes the temperature is decreasing at about 3 degrees Celsius per minute.}

points.criterion: States that at t = 5 minutes the coffee's temperature is changing at the presented rate (decreasing at about 3 degrees Celsius per minute for -3), naming the quantity, the rate with units and the instant, with sign language consistent with the presented value.
